details.expected: Requirements. Where two vehicle paths cross, the general rule is to yield to a vehicle approaching from your right, except where another applicable rule or instruction determines the relationship. Road width, familiarity or the fact that you are travelling straight does not by itself establish priority. Right-hand priority can apply at a three-way junction or within a parking area. Right-hand priority · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §18

details.expected: Different duties apply when entering a road from premises, a car park, fuel station, similar roadside area, path or similar exit, or from terrain, a pedestrian street, walking-speed area or cycle street. After crossing a footway or cycle path to enter a road, the exit provision also matters. Do not decide solely from a kerb's appearance; identify the actual layout. Joining a priority road without an acceleration lane generally requires yielding, subject to the provision for joining without changing lane. Roundabout entry has its own duty. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§21–23

details.expected: Requirements. Before a turn, check that it will not obstruct oncoming traffic or traffic on the road you are entering. Pay attention to people travelling in the same direction, including those behind you. Position early: normally the right-hand lane for a right turn and the left-hand lane for a left turn where multiple approach lanes exist, subject to applicable signs, markings and space provisions. On a two-way road, a left turn is normally prepared near the road centre; on a one-way carriageway, near the left edge. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24–29

details.expected: For a lane change or significant sideways movement, signal clearly and in time, then check that the movement can be made without danger or unnecessary obstruction. The indicator announces an intention, not a claim on a gap. Drivers who notice another vehicle intending to join their lane must adjust speed to help; when two lanes merge into one, both drivers must adapt with mutual consideration. These duties work together. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§43–44 and 65–66

details.expected: Safety advice · Wait with front wheels straight. When stopped waiting to turn left across oncoming traffic, keep your front wheels pointing straight ahead. Your indicator communicates the intended turn; your wheels do not need to point along that intended route while you wait. If a vehicle hits you from behind, front wheels already turned left can direct the pushed car into oncoming traffic. Keeping them straight helps reduce that risk, but cannot guarantee protection in a collision. Begin steering into the turn only when there is a safe opportunity to make it. New York DMV: waiting to turn left

details.expected: Requirements. At an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, yield to pedestrians who are on it or about to enter. Someone walking a bicycle is a pedestrian; someone riding one is not made a pedestrian merely by using the painted crossing. A person using a wheelchair at walking speed is covered by pedestrian rules. This distinction never removes the general duty to avoid danger. Pedestrian crossings · Wheelchair users · Traffic Regulation, chapter 1 §4 and chapter 3 §61

Road width, familiarity or the fact that you are travelling straight does not by itself establish priority. Right-hand priority can apply at a three-way junction or within a parking area. Right-hand priority · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §18

expected_segments: Different duties apply when entering a road from premises, a car park, fuel station, similar roadside area, path or similar exit, or from terrain, a pedestrian street, walking-speed area or cycle street. After crossing a footway or cycle path to enter a road, the exit provision also matters. Do not decide solely from a kerb's appearance; identify the actual layout. Joining a priority road without an acceleration lane generally requires yielding, subject to the provision for joining without changing lane. Roundabout entry has its own duty. expected_segments: Requirements. Before a turn, check that it will not obstruct oncoming traffic or traffic on the road you are entering. Pay attention to people travelling in the same direction, including those behind you. Position early: normally the right-hand lane for a right turn and the left-hand lane for a left turn where multiple approach lanes exist, subject to applicable signs, markings and space provisions. On a two-way road, a left turn is normally prepared near the road centre; on a one-way carriageway, near the left edge. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24–29

checks.name: M04-L02/teaching-005 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Safety advice · Wait with front wheels straight. When stopped waiting to turn left across oncoming traffic, keep your front wheels pointing straight ahead. Your indicator communicates the intended turn; your wheels do not need to point along that intended route while you wait. If a vehicle hits you from behind, front wheels already turned left can direct the pushed car into oncoming traffic. Keeping them straight helps reduce that risk, but cannot guarantee protection in a collision. Begin steering into the turn only when there is a safe opportunity to make it. New York DMV: waiting to turn left

checks.name: M04-L02/teaching-006 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Waiting is different from turning. Follow the positioning, signalling and observation requirements above. The wheel-position advice does not create permission to enter or block a junction, ignore a signal, or obstruct someone else's path. Continue observing oncoming traffic, the receiving road, crossings and vehicles behind you while waiting. Recheck the full path before moving.

checks.name: M04-L02/teaching-007 reader content and answer reveal

On rural roads, use M06-L01 to assess bends, crests and other risks before choosing a turning opportunity.

checks.name: M04-L04/teaching-002 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Requirements. Travel anticlockwise and yield on entry to vehicles already circulating. Choose an appropriate lane for the onward route and obey signs and markings. There is no general requirement to signal solely for entering; signal lane changes and significant sideways movements, and signal right when leaving. Any lane change must be safe and must not create unnecessary obstruction. Transportstyrelsen: roundabout guide · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§13, 22, 43 and 65–66

checks.name: M04-L04/teaching-003 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Learning approach. Read the layout before reaching the yield point. Reduce speed enough to judge circulating traffic and the available space. Observe crossings on the approach as separate conflicts. Inside, hold your intended path and continue checking nearby vehicles. A large vehicle may need more room than its apparent lane width suggests. Roundabout guide

checks.name: M04-L04/teaching-004 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Plan the exit early. Moving from an inner lane across an outer lane is a lane change, even though you call the whole movement “leaving the roundabout.” Do not assume a vehicle beside you will leave at the same exit. If the exit cannot be taken safely, continue as the layout allows and re-plan. On leaving, check the crossing area again; the duties in M04-L03 still apply. Roundabout guide · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§60–62
